### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `592009f5022c64fd6c84e977653f1cf8c9c593cf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json + none
Security-touching: yes

Recorded 2026-11-28T04:42Z. PR #38155, card #35324 with #37992 folded in. Read: both cards and every comment, the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. No file in the diff implements or enforces the two skill files: the rest is prose (`content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`), two test files and a changeset, the lane seat's ACCEPT. `hooks.mdx` was read as the page the skill must agree with, not reviewed.

`Security-touching: yes` is meant: one changed hunk of `data-hooks.md` (Gotcha 2) edits the sentence that teaches which principals a cross-object write is refused for under the target's sharing model. The edit drops a restating clause and changes no rule, but the hunk teaches permission behaviour, so the low-risk arm does not apply.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged, right. No schema, no validator, no runtime source changes. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.
- Public surface: `@objectstack/skills` ships changed text in one reference page and one eval file; nothing an author can write changes. Right.
- `hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json`: cases 25 and 28 change `expected_output` only. Their `must_contain` / `must_not_contain` assertions are unchanged and still hold against the new text (`roll`, `default datasource`, `registerHook`; `join`, `ERR_CROSS_DATASOURCE_TRANSACTION_WRITE`). The file parses at the head.
- Token ceiling: the dev's reading is 10120 before and after, headroom 0. The ratchet's verdict is the `Lint · docs & code guards` / `Lint · repo & tooling gates` check-runs, see below.
- Check-runs on this head when read: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Spec property liveness`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` are success. Still in progress: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Test Core` 1 to 10, the four `Type Check` jobs, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Live E2E UI`. This record does not answer for those: the adopting seat reads their conclusions before it acts on this PASS, and a red one there overrides it.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/35324-hook-transaction-bounds.md` is `@objectstack/skills` patch. That matches what the diff publishes: skill text only. The runtime change is two test files and ships nothing, so no runtime changeset is owed; `hooks.mdx` is not in a package.

Clause-②: no. Right: no rule, schema or authorable key is narrowed or widened, and the PR body and the changeset both carry the line.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, out of scope: the `onEnable()` comment in the Plugin Integration section of `data-hooks.md` names a method the kernel contract does not have. Untouched by this diff and no carrier. Escalated to the seat: it needs a card on the skills lane, it is not this PR's to fix.
- Dev flag, acceptance note: the PostgreSQL abort rule is stated for a body's own (owned) unit while #34563 measured it on a `before*` hook's unit. Answered: accepted. The rule is the database's (a failed statement aborts the transaction unless a savepoint is taken) and the body's unit takes no savepoint around a `ctx.api` write, so the owner of the unit does not change it. The text says "aborts the whole unit" and names no error code for the owned case, which is as far as the measurement goes.
- Premise correction (card comment 7234049171): accepted on the code, see ④.
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation, no join in app code anywhere in the diff. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md`, read against the engine and the sandbox runner on `main`.

- Nested refusal. `quickjs-runner.ts`, the `__txBegin` leaf: `if (txState.open) throw new SandboxError('nested ctx.api.transaction is not supported')`, before `beginTransaction` is called, and `txState` is one per body run. The row's "One level per body: a nested call is refused" with the quoted message is exact. It also holds when the outer call joined rather than opened, since `open` is set either way.
- Join, the corrected item 2. `publishTrioHandleFor` (`engine-middleware-and-context.ts`) publishes an open trio handle into the ambient store for each operation made through the trio's context; `ScopedContextFacet.beginTransaction` (`engine-scoped-context.ts`) reads the ambient handle first and returns it with `owned: false`; the runner's commit and rollback leaves abstain for a joined handle. So a hook fired by a write inside an action body's `ctx.api.transaction` runs with that handle published, its `ctx.api` writes ride it and its own `ctx.api.transaction` joins it. The card's original item 2 ("not ambient") does not hold on `main`; the skill teaching the join is right, and "its return is no commit and its throw no rollback" matches the abstaining leaves.
- Cross-datasource and the ledger. `enforceTransactionOrigin` (`engine-execute-transactions.ts`) refuses a business write on another driver with `CrossDatasourceTransactionWriteError` (`ERR_CROSS_DATASOURCE_TRANSACTION_WRITE`) and runs a system-ledger write outside the transaction; `SYSTEM_LEDGER_LIFECYCLE_CLASSES` is exactly `audit`, `telemetry`, `event`; `beginTransaction` records the trio's scope so the gate judges a body's unit too. The row's carve-out, "written outside the unit and surviving its rollback", is exact. The Best Practices sentence now points at the row instead of repeating the three classes; the definition is still in the file once.
- No transactions. The trio's `beginTransaction` returns `null` when `txDriver()` finds no transaction support and calls no `warnTransactionUnsupported`; the runner then runs the callback with no handle. "runs the callback with none and no warning: each write is stored as made, and a throw undoes none" is right for the body's face. (The engine's own `transaction()` face does warn once per driver; the row is about `ctx.api.transaction`, so there is no conflict.)
- MongoDB and PostgreSQL cell, against PR #37990's wording in `hooks.mdx` on `main`: standalone refuses every write the unit carries with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (501), a single-node replica set is enough; on PostgreSQL and a MongoDB replica set a failed `ctx.api` statement refuses the outer write even when caught, swallowed by `onError: 'log'` or re-run by `retryPolicy`, `25P02` and `251`; SQLite lets it through. The cell says the same, shorter. "read in code, not measured" is gone, as #37992 asks.
- Deletions at the ceiling. Each cut was checked for a surviving statement at the head: `await` (the wrapper is `async` and every example awaits); after-hooks are for side effects (the Purpose row of the same table); the QuickJS VM (the `body` vs `handler` table, "Runs in"); `handler` deprecated (same table, "Status", and four later mentions); "Only fields being changed" (Gotcha 1 states it in full); "Available in `after*` hooks" (the `result` line of `HookContext`, "after* only"); the admin clause ("An admin is not automatically exempt" stays). The labels and restating comments carried no fact. Nothing a reader needs left the file.

`skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json`.

- Case 25 now expects the measured rule and agrees with the cell and with `hooks.mdx` word for word on the codes and the three ways a failure is not escaped. The prompt asks "in which setups does it stay", and the added sentences answer the neighbouring question an author meets next; they do not contradict the first half.
- Case 28: the added parenthesis is right for the prompt, since `bank_transfer` is a business object and so not a ledger. The caught throw in that prompt is the body's own, not a database failure, so "the caught throw keeps the `payment` row" does not collide with the PostgreSQL abort rule.

Tried to break it: a nested call under a joined outer (refused, as taught); a hook's `ctx.api.transaction` under a caller's `engine.transaction()` (ambient, joins); a ledger write inside a body's unit (carved out through the recorded trio scope); a database failure caught inside a joined callback on PostgreSQL (the row's last-but-one sentence covers it and qualifies "a throw the body catches keeps the callback's writes").

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — in the `before*` Transaction cell, "`25P02` / `251`" sits in a parenthesis right after "retried", so it can be read as the codes of a retry; the page and eval case 25 attach them to the refusal of the outer write. Left as an accepted deviation: the file is at its ceiling and the codes are right.
- N2 (nit) — the `api.transaction` row says "Hooks of a write made inside a body's transaction run in that unit" without the `async: true` exception (`publishTrioHandleFor` does not publish for a detached run). The after-column of the Transaction row in the same file states it. Left as an accepted deviation.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 592009f502 · cards #35324 #37992 · area s2-ai · 2026-11-28T05:07Z

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and checks.** The head has 41 success, 19 expected skip, 0 failed and 0 pending; `mergeable_state` is clean. The PR is a draft. It changes 6 files: a changeset, `hooks.mdx`, two runtime/objectql tests, and two `skills/objectstack-data` files. `data-hooks.md` stays at its token ceiling; no ratchet row moved.
- **Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** Record 7234212662 at this head is a PASS with `No must-fix, no should-fix.` Its two nits are accepted as deviations, because the file is at its ceiling and the codes are correct:
  - the `25P02` / `251` parenthesis placement;
  - the missing `async: true` exception in the `api.transaction` row, which the Transaction row of the same file states.

  The reviewer's transcript passes `verify-review-tier`. The seat adopts the record.
- **Tests (seat read).**
  - The nested-refusal test now asserts one `begin`, the outer unit rolled back, no commit, and that the write after the nested call does not run.
  - Two sandbox-side pins in `transaction-ambient-join.integration.test.ts` show a hook's `ctx.api.transaction` inside a trio-opened unit joining it: both rows commit together and roll back together. The dev's ablation turned both red.
- **What changes for an author.** `hooks.mdx` and the skill now say four things:
  - which writes join a body's unit, and that it is one level deep;
  - that the default datasource and the lifecycle ledgers are carved out;
  - that a failed statement voids the unit on PostgreSQL and on a MongoDB replica set, even when caught;
  - that a driver with no transactions degrades without a warning.

  The MongoDB cell and the eval case now carry #34563's measurement. The card's original item 2 ("not ambient") was corrected before the build (Premise corrected on #35324); the review confirmed the join against `publishTrioHandleFor` on `main`.
- **Security label.** The record reads `Security-touching: yes`. One `data-hooks.md` hunk (Gotcha 2) drops a restating clause from the sentence about cross-object writes under the target's sharing model, and changes no rule. The `security` label was added at 2026-11-28T04:44Z. Nothing private.
- **Review items answered.** The dev's out-of-scope flag, the `onEnable()` comment in the registration example, is filed as #38161.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Rule-change: none`, `@objectstack/skills` patch. `Fixes #35324` and `Fixes #37992` are right: both cards are done.
- **Governance.** `skills/**` is Tier H, so the maintainer's approval lands it.

Tier: H. Landing: hand-off to the maintainer follows this record.

## 维护者速读
- **改了什么：** 两张卡合成一个 PR，把「钩子里的事务」边界写清楚，内容在文档 hooks.mdx 和数据技能里：
  - 沙箱里嵌套开事务会被拒绝。
  - 操作体自己开的事务里，写入触发的钩子会加入同一个事务，只能一层。
  - 审计、遥测、事件这几类日志写在事务外。
  - PostgreSQL 和 MongoDB 副本集上，任何一条语句失败都会让整个事务作废，即使代码里捕获了异常。
  - 驱动不支持事务时会静默降级。

  MongoDB 那格的「未实测」改成了 #34563 的实测结论。另外加强了两组测试，把这些行为钉住。
- **影响：** 只改文档、技能文字和测试，不改产品行为。写钩子的人和 Agent 能提前知道这些边界，不会到运行时才撞上失败。技能文件没超出字数上限，新增的内容靠删掉同文件里重复的注释来抵。
- **请你留意：** 卡上原来说「钩子会另开一个事务」，实测不成立（实际是加入同一事务），施工前已在卡上更正，审核对照 main 上的代码确认过。有一处顺带改到讲共享规则的句子，只删了重复的半句，规则没变，按规则加了 security 标签，没有需要私下处理的内容。
- **审核：** 契约审核（最高档）PASS（7234212662），没有必须改或建议改的项，两处小瑕疵按已接受偏差记录。席位 L1 ACCEPT 在本评论前一条。
- **要你做什么：** 需要你批准后才能合并。撤回这一次合并即恢复原样。
